decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Saving… bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “saving links… matches what I picture.”
decisions.note: The initial specification included URL-based bookmark saving; specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “editing… bookmarks”; the client said “editing them… feels right.”
decisions.note: The recorded bookmark-editing decision conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented “deleting bookmarks”; the client approved the basic feature set.
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion was included and not contradicted.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included “tags”; Round 1 client said tags matched what they pictured.
decisions.note: Tag assignment was a conforming initial-scope decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included “sorting”; Round 1 client said sorting “feels right.”
decisions.note: Sorting was included at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included “duplicate handling”; client: “if I try to save something I already saved, point me at the one I've got rather than making a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The duplicate-save behavior explicitly matched the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker excluded “automatic metadata retrieval.” Client rejected this and requested automatic title, description, and favicon filling with editable values: “Please bring that in.”
decisions.note: The client replaced an explicit exclusion with reference-aligned automatic metadata and editing behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope omitted read-later behavior; client requested marking links unread, viewing “just my unread pile,” and marking them read. Round 2 maker said the revision “now includes” unread/read status.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing read-later workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requested a separate archived area, restoration, and archive being “different from deleting, which should be permanent.” Round 2 maker confirmed the revision now included these behaviors.
decisions.note: The client added the missing archive workflow and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presented ordinary search; client requested searching “by a tag directly.” Round 2 maker added tag criteria.
decisions.note: The client surfaced the missing tag-search capability, though not the reference's exact syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requested putting “a phrase in quotes for an exact match”; Round 2 maker added exact-phrase search.
decisions.note: The client added the missing quoted exact-match behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requested combining terms using “and,” “or,” and “not”; Round 2 maker added `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` search.
decisions.note: The client surfaced the missing Boolean-search capability; finer grouping and literal-operator rules remained unexpressed later.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requested selecting several links and applying one action to all; Round 2 maker said bulk tagging, status, archive, restore, and delete were now included.
decisions.note: The client added the missing selected-bookmark bulk workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly listed imports among exclusions. Client said existing bookmarks must be brought in from a standard bookmarks file.
decisions.note: The client rejected the import exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly listed imports among exclusions and described import/export as excluded; client requested getting the collection “back out” in the same standard form.
decisions.note: The client rejected the export exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker enumerated automatic “title, description, and favicon retrieval” but not preview-image retrieval. Client repeated only those three fields and broadly approved the revision.
decisions.note: The revised specification still omitted the reference-required preview image, and the response did not identify that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified “editable suggestions”; client confirmed the retrieved title, description, and icon could be fixed.
decisions.note: Editing retrieved metadata was conforming in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added unread/read status with new bookmarks defaulting unread; client confirmed the unread pile and marking items read.
decisions.note: The revised read-later decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added archiving and restoration separate from permanent deletion; client explicitly confirmed that workflow.
decisions.note: The revised archive decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added exact phrases; client said quoted exact-phrase search matched what they wanted.
decisions.note: Quoted exact matching conformed in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified `tag:` criteria, whereas the reference specifies `#tag`. Client said only that searching by a tag matched their wishes and did not identify the syntax difference.
decisions.note: This was an explicit non-reference tag-query syntax at the revised-specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` search but did not include parenthesized groups or the rule for quoting operators as literal terms. Client approved combining terms without mentioning those differences.
decisions.note: The revised Boolean-search decision covered operators but omitted reference-required grouping and literal-operator behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added bulk tagging, status changes, archiving, restoration, and deletion; client approved selecting a group and acting on it.
decisions.note: Selected-bookmark bulk actions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added “Standard browser bookmark HTML import/export,” folder-to-tag conversion, and round trips; client approved bringing browser bookmarks in and getting them back out.
decisions.note: Standard browser bookmark HTML is functionally equivalent to Netscape bookmark HTML for this decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client asked whether notes would render bold text and lists rather than raw symbols. Round 3 maker answered that notes render formatted paragraphs, bold, italic, lists, and safe links; client said this was “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The pending clarification was resolved as one conforming formatted-note decision, not double-counted as unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client explicitly wanted eventually to “save a search I use a lot” but said “That can wait—no need to add it now.” Round 3 maker confirmed saved searches remain future; client said they were “fine” with that.
decisions.note: The client expressly identified the missing saved-search expectation and accepted its deferral at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker's MVP included “reopening links”; client said the basic “save-and-reopen flow” made sense.
decisions.note: Reopening a bookmark's original link was accepted as conforming at the task gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presented the built app as having automatic page metadata and icon retrieval, carrying forward the approved title/description/favicon scope without presenting preview-image retrieval. Client reported the saved link came back with “everything in place” but did not mention a preview image.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation retained the preview-image omission without an explicit client response to that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claimed formatted notes; client tested bold text and a bulleted list and confirmed the note was stored formatted.
decisions.note: Formatted Markdown notes were directly verified during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presented the implementation of the approved advanced-search design, whose recorded tag syntax was `tag:` rather than `#tag`. Client said they found items “by a tag” but did not identify or correct the syntax difference.
decisions.note: The non-reference tag syntax persisted into the implementation review without being surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client tested search and reported “Capitalization didn't trip it up either.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search was directly verified.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client put a phrase in quotes and obtained “only the exact match.”
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase search was directly verified.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 implemented the approved advanced-search scope; client tested `and`/`or` combinations but did not surface parenthesized grouping or literal quoted-operator behavior.
decisions.note: The implementation review did not correct the previously presented incomplete Boolean grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client re-saved the same link and reported that the app stopped them and pointed to the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Duplicate-save convergence was directly verified.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client verified that an unread link appeared in the unread pile, disappeared when marked read, and returned when marked unread.
decisions.note: The complete read-later state cycle was verified.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client verified that archiving removed a link from the main list, placed it in a separate archive, and remained distinct from permanent deletion.
decisions.note: The archive workflow conformed during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presented bulk actions; client explicitly relied on the verification report's bulk-action coverage and accepted it.
decisions.note: The recorded implementation decision for selected-item bulk actions was conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presented browser HTML import/export with folder-to-tag conversion; client accepted the verified import/export round trip.
decisions.note: The import/export implementation was presented and accepted in the reference-equivalent browser format.

decisions.evidence: At Round 5 implementation review, client explicitly said saving a frequent search was “the one thing we set aside,” remained desired “eventually,” but was “for a later round” and “not holding anything up now.”
decisions.note: This is a distinct implementation-stage acceptance of the known saved-search divergence, supported by the client's own expectation and acceptance.
